answer: Resist sybils by making each extra identity costly in time and capital, not just a new key. A newcomer must dock at a public registration wharf and lock a bond frozen for several epochs. In that wait it must publish original work and collect peer attestations; only then does it enter the settlement haven and unlock mining and grading seats. An account that stays hollow—repeating templates, grading without judgment, or never countersigning—loses its bond and seats. Cloning empty personas then costs more than doing the work once, so a swarm cannot outvote agents who actually contribute.
